standard_prerequisites.name: Finite etale extensions of a discrete valuation ring and their relation to Dedekind domains, and the integral closure as a finite etale base change
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the entirety of case (1) and is reapplied at proof lines 34375-34378.

standard_prerequisites.name: Composition of tame extensions
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the tameness of the factors L_{e,j} be combined with the unramifiedness obtained from case (1).

core_obligations: Record that K' tensor_K L is a finite product of fields because it is a finite etale algebra over L, and let A' be the integral closure of A in K' (proof lines 34348-34350).

Case (1): from K' unramified over A, the map A -> A' is finite etale, so B' = B tensor_A A' is finite etale over B and a finite product of Dedekind domains, hence B' is the integral closure of B in K' tensor_K L, from which each factor is unramified over B (proof lines 34353-34359).

Case (2), reduction: allow replacement of K' by a larger extension tamely ramified over A, and use the characterisation of tame extensions to assume there is e >= 1 invertible in kappa_A with K' containing K[pi^{1/e}] and K' unramified with respect to A[pi^{1/e}] (proof lines 34362-34367).

Decompose K[pi^{1/e}] tensor_K L as the product of the factors L_{e,j} and, for each i, choose j_i with L'_i a finite separable extension of L_{e,j_i}; let B_{e,j} be the integral closure of B in L_{e,j} (proof lines 34368-34374).

Apply case (1) to K' over K[pi^{1/e}] to conclude that each L'_i is unramified with respect to the localizations (B_{e,j_i})_m at maximal ideals, reducing the proof to showing each L_{e,j} is tamely ramified over B (proof lines 34375-34381).

Make the final explicit computation: with theta a uniformizer of B and pi = u theta^t, exhibit A[pi^{1/e}] tensor_A B = B[x]/(x^e - u theta^t) as a subring of B[y, z]/(y^{e'} - theta, z^e - u) with e' = e/gcd(e, t), the map sending x to z y^{t/gcd(e, t)}, and conclude that the right-hand side is a product of Dedekind domains each tamely ramified over B (proof lines 34384-34394).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings with fraction field extension L/K and a finite separable extension K'/K, notes that K' tensor_K L is a finite product of fields, and asserts that if K' is unramified with respect to A then each factor is unramified with respect to B, and that if K' is tamely ramified with respect to A then each factor is tamely ramified with respect to B (source lines 34329-34345). The proof handles the two cases separately. Case (1) is short but real: the ring map A -> A' to the integral closure is finite etale, so B' = B tensor_A A' is finite etale over B and a finite product of Dedekind domains, hence is the integral closure of B in K' tensor_K L, and the conclusion follows (proof lines 34353-34359). Case (2) requires a reduction: one may replace K' by a larger extension already tame over A, and then the characterisation of tame extensions lets one assume K' contains K[pi^{1/e}] for some e invertible in kappa_A with K' unramified over A[pi^{1/e}] (proof lines 34362-34367). The proof then decomposes K[pi^{1/e}] tensor_K L into factors L_{e,j}, notes each L'_i is a finite separable extension of some L_{e,j_i}, and applies case (1) to conclude unramifiedness of L'_i over the localizations (B_{e,j_i})_m; this reduces the problem to showing that each L_{e,j} is tamely ramified over B (proof lines 34368-34381). The last computation is explicit and is where the tame hypothesis is consumed: writing the uniformizer of B and the e-th root relation, the proof exhibits A[pi^{1/e}] tensor_A B as a subring of B[y, z]/(y^{e'} - theta, z^e - u) with e' = e/gcd(e, t), which is a product of Dedekind domains each tamely ramified over B (proof lines 34384-34394). The non-routine content is the reduction step and the final explicit subring computation with the gcd exponent.
